judgment.rationale: Both are Performance Objectives under the same Topic (2. Length), Sub-Theme (Primary Measures), Theme (Mensuration and Geometry), and Grade (PRIMARY TWO), same rank. The second SFI (385b944a) has pupils compare natural/non-standard units of length (e.g. arm's length), while the first SFI (1e15584c) has pupils use metres and centimetres as standard measuring units. Experiencing and comparing natural units and their variability pedagogically motivates and supports the transition to formal standard units, so proficiency in the second supports success in the first. This is a substantive developmental progression (natural-to-standard units), not mere shared hierarchy or wording; hence buildsTowards second_to_first rather than relatesTo.

First objective is 'identify the relationship between addition and subtraction'; second is 'find missing number in an open sentence'. These are conceptually coherent, complementary skills within the same open-sentences topic: understanding the inverse addition/subtraction relationship reinforces solving open sentences for a missing number and vice versa. producer_judgment.rationale: Both are PRIMARY ONE Performance Objectives under the same Theme (Number and Numeration) / Sub-Theme (Whole Number). The second SFI (c4885674) is 'Count and read correctly from 1-9' (Topic 3, Whole numbers 6-9), while the first SFI (2bb1227e) is 'identify and read correctly the numbers 1-99' (Topic 5, Whole Numbers 1-99). Reading/counting the smaller range 1-9 is a foundational component whose mastery supports success in identifying and reading the broader 1-99 range; the source-topic sequence (Topic 3 before Topic 5) and the LC 'read correctly' overlap support this substantive broadening rather than mere repetition. Same-rank direction is justified by the subset-to-broader-range extension, giving source=1-9 (second) building toward target=1-99 (first).
